ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AD \perp BC$ at point $D$, $\cos B = \frac{4}{5}$, $\tan C = \sqrt{3}$, $AB = 5$. Find the length of $AC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}\\
Since $AD\perp BC$,\\
it follows that $\angle ADB=\angle ADC=90^\circ$,\\
Since $\cos B=\frac{4}{5}$ and $AB=5$,\\
it follows that $BD=AB\cdot\cos B=5\times \frac{4}{5}=4$,\\
Therefore, $AD=\sqrt{AB^{2}-BD^{2}}=\sqrt{5^{2}-4^{2}}=3$,\\
Since $\tan C=\sqrt{3}$,\\
it follows that $CD=\frac{AD}{\tan C}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}}=\sqrt{3}$,\\
Therefore, $AC=\sqrt{AD^{2}+CD^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}+(\sqrt{3})^{2}}=\boxed{2\sqrt{3}}$.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: the image shows triangle ABC with A above the base BC, point D on segment BC, and AD drawn perpendicular to BC, forming two right triangles ABD and ACD. Use the text givens cos B = 4/5 and AB = 5 in right triangle ABD: cos B = adjacent/hypotenuse = BD/AB, so BD = 4. Then use the Pythagorean theorem to get AD = sqrt(AB^2 - BD^2) = 3. In right triangle ACD, use tan C = opposite/adjacent = AD/CD = sqrt(3), so CD = AD/sqrt(3) = sqrt(3). Finally compute AC as the hypotenuse of right triangle ACD: AC = sqrt(AD^2 + CD^2) = 2sqrt(3).
